Commentary.Commentary: Right. Confused? We feel that the pitch is on the slower side and 272 may not be the easiest of run chases. Lungi Ngidi feels that the track is a good one to bat on. Stay tuned to see how the run chase actually pans out.

Lungi Ngidi says that he has been feeling well over the last few weeks and today, he just tried to stick to his basics and is happy that he did well. Adds that he had a chat with coach Mark Boucher before the game and the goal was to knock over the big three (Warner, Finch and Smith). Praises the bowlers for bowling well in Powerplay 1 and the spinners for maintaining the pressure, which helped him. Rates the pitch as a good one to bat on with probably just a few holes here and there. Reckons that taking wickets is certainly not going to be easy on this deck.

What can we read from the last sentence of the previous paragraph? Does it mean that the bowling was extremely good? Or does it indicate that the pitch has gotten slow? The Proteas mixed their pace really nicely but the Aussie made no attempt whatsoever to try and gauge the conditions. That also means that it is difficult for a new batsman to hit from the word go. Lungi Ngidi was the pick of the bowlers, with 6/58 but he received good support from Andile Phehlukwayo whose 1/44 kept the tourists quiet. Here is Ngidi, talking to Mike Haysman.

Australia were motoring along at nearly 7 an over but now had to rebuild. Aaron Finch found an able ally in D'Arcy Short and their 77-run stand got Australia on the road to recovery. That was followed by another 66-run stand but after that, the Kangaroos lost their way. At 222/4 in 40 overs, they should have got close to 300 but they have not even reached 275. Powerplay 3 yielded just 49 runs and resulted in 6 wickets.

Australia started like a train on fire, without any brakes. They ran and ran, like there is no tomorrow, putting the Proteas under the pump. But eventually, as they say, if you live by the sword, you die by it as well. David Warner was dismissed, after playing an array of strokes and for a change, both master and disciple flopped. Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne were dismissed off successive deliveries and that changed the course of the innings.

272 to win for South Africa to wrap up the series here itself. Possible? Difficult? A bit of both. 272 is not the tallest target in the world but the deck is not the best to bat on either. To cut it short, we are in for a wonderful run chase.

FOUR! Another example of power. Full and on  off, Warner whacks it over mid off and the ball goes off a couple of bounces and into the fence there.
Short of a length ball on off, Finch drops it towards mid on and hares for a run. In the end the batters get one.
Length and on off, Finch defends it off the back foot to covers.
Length ball on off, Warner taps it to point for a run.
Full and angled across the batter, Warner plays it through point and takes a couple this time.
Once again bowled on a length and on off, Finch plays it to covers.
Length ball on off, Finch pushes it to covers.
FOUR! That's stand and deliver stuff for Finch. Ngidi bowls one on a length and wide outside off, Finch lofts it over covers and the ball races to the fence in no time.
FOUR! Sheer timing. Ngidi bowls one on the pads of Finch and Aaron there just flicks it towards mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full delivery on off, Warner drives it towards mid off for a single.
On a length on middle, Finch flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
Lungi Ngidi is on.
Length ball on pads, Finch tucks it towards the leg side for a single.
Full and on around off, pushed to point.
Length and on off, Finch blocks it off the back foot.
Full and on off, Warner punches the ball off the back foot through covers for a single.

SIX! First maximum. How big a ground you prepare Warner is going to find the fence with ease. Short and on middle, Warner pulls it but not off the middle of the bat as the ball goes off the top edge towards fine leg for a biggie.
Short of a length ball outside off, Warner slaps it towards covers.
On middle, Finch keeps it out.
Tossed up delivery on off, Finch lofts it over mid off. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Loopy delivery on off, Finch defends it off the front foot.
Flighted delivery on off, Warner drives it towards mid off for a single.
FOUR! Nice shot! Full delivery on off, Warner drives it through covers for a boundary.
Tossed up delivery on off, Warner drives it to covers.

Ohh! That was close. Had Finch missed that one, he would have been a goner. Nortje bowls one on a length and gets it to tail back into the batter. Finch is late in bringing his bat down in time and ekes out an inside edge onto the pads.
Short of a length ball on middle, Warner pulls it towards mid-wicket where the fielder misfields to allow a single.
Full and on off, Warner punches the ball off the back foot towards covers.
Length and on off, Warner flicks it to mid-wicket for a couple.
OHH! That's a ripper! Nortje lands one on a length and on off, Warner is cut into half as he looks to defend it off the back foot. The ball sneaks between the bat and the body towards keeper.
FOUR! Smashed! Warner is not going to miss on that. Nortje bowls one wide outside off, Warner leans and drives it through covers to get a boundary.
Anrich Nortje to bowl from the other end.
Full and on middle, flicked towards mid-wicket for a run. 5 runs off the first over of Maharaj.
Flatter and on off, Warner blocks it off the back foot.
Floated on off, Finch drops it towards point and gets off the mark with a single.
Full and on off, Warner pushes it off the front foot but gets it off the outside edge towards point for a run.
Floated on off, pushed towards mid-wicket.
Maharaj starts with a flatter one outside off, Warner flashes at it to get a thick outside edge towards third man for a couple.  Warner and Australia are off the mark.

We are all set for the action to begin. The South African players are out in the middle. Temba Bavuma has been ruled out due to an injury to his  right hamstring. Rassie van der Dussen has been included as his replacement for the remainder of the series. Aaron Finch and David Warner will open the batting for Australia. Keshav Maharaj will start the proceedings for South Africa.

South African skipper, Quinton de Kock says that he is not sure how the wicket will play. On South Africa's great record at this venue, Quinny replies that they are not reading too much into the numbers as they take one game at a time. Composure is the key, adds the skipper. Confirms that Temba Bavuma is out injured and JJ Smuts has replaced him.

Australian skipper, Aaron Finch says that they are batting as the wicket is appearing to be dry and it may slow down later on. Further says that they are learning from their mistakes and would like to work on it. Informs that Ashton Agar is replacing Josh Hazlewood as the conditions will assist the spinners.

South Africa Playing XI - Quinton de Kock (C/WK), Janneman Malan, JJ Smuts (In for Temba Bavuma), Kyle Verreynne, Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Andile Phehlukwayo, Keshav Maharaj, Anrich Nortje, Lungi Ngidi, Tabraiz Shamsi.

Australia Playing XI - David Warner, Aaron Finch (C), Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, D'Arcy Short, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, Adam Zampa, Ashton Agar (In for Josh Hazlewood).
TOSS - It's time for the flip of the coin. Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Aaron Finch. AUSTRALIA WIN THE TOSS AND ELECT TO BAT!

After winning the first ODI at Paarl, the hosts would be high on confidence going ahead in the second ODI. South Africa powered to a total close to 300 courtesy of a maiden ODI ton from Heinrich Klaasen. Then their bowlers bowled superbly to restrict Australia to take a 1-0 lead in the 3-match series. However, going by the last 4 series, South Africa have failed to win the series after taking the lead. They would look to reverse that trend and seal the series here itself. On the other hand, Australia would come harder at the Proteas after the defeat and would look to win and take the series to a decider. A cracker of a contest awaits as we are not far away from the toss and the team news. Hello and welcome to the second ODI.
